content_units: A strong 4-film lineup for 5 adults is   “Reality, Identity, and Human Connection”  : start playful and accessible, move into sharper questions about memory and truth, then end with emotionally rich discussion fuel. This mix stays   under 9 hours including two 30-minute breaks  , spans   multiple genres  , and avoids extreme violence.
Order   Film   Genre   Runtime   Why it fits the arc
1     The Truman Show   (1998)   Satirical drama / sci-fi   1h 43m   A light, witty opener about constructed reality and personal freedom.
2     Arrival   (2016)   Sci-fi / drama   1h 56m   Expands the theme from personal reality to language, time, and understanding others.
3     Her   (2013)   Romantic drama / sci-fi   2h 6m   Turns the focus inward to intimacy, technology, and what makes connection real.
4     Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind   (2004)   Romance / psychological drama / sci-fi   1h 48m   A reflective closer on memory, pain, and whether love is worth repeating.
-   Start accessible:    The Truman Show  is funny, warm, and easy to settle into as a group.
-   Broaden the ideas:    Arrival  raises the intellectual stakes without becoming harsh or violent.
-   Deepen the emotional layer:    Her  makes the conversation more personal and modern.
-   End on the richest discussion piece:    Eternal Sunshine  leaves the room with questions about memory, regret, and choice.
This creates a clean arc from   external reality → perception and time → emotional intimacy → memory and love  .
-   Film 4:    Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind  — 1h 48m
If watched straight through, the full program runs   8 hours 33 minutes  .
Option 1:   Best overall lineup     Balanced, smart, emotional, and conversation-friendly     3 sci-fi-inflected films + 1 satirical drama
Option 2:   Why it suits your group     Works well for 5 adults because the tone evolves without becoming too heavy too fast     Low gore, high discussion payoff
Option 3:   Post-movie conversation starters     “What makes something real?”, “Can memory be trusted?”, “Is pain necessary for love?”     Strong after-screening discussion
